craft_notes: Sthāyin: vastness yielding plainness. Sanskrit-first: vitataḥ (SPREAD — vastness as action, doctrine not décor) + naiva śakyate (not-possible AT ALL) + śṛṇuta (LISTEN! 2pl imperative — the song commands). Abhinavagupta frame: the ocean-to-essence move (unplungeable → plain words) is the whole Tantrasāra's apology and method. Rows: 5 (anastrophe ‘Wide spreads’ — hymn-opening inversion; word order freed for music, trace unchanged; bank: Holcombe word-order-in-joints), 1 (viracitam end-weighted — ‘composed’: made-ness as destination, the book IS the making). Close: ‘in plain words composed’. Rejected: ‘vast’ for ‘spreads wide’ — killed: vitataḥ acts; ‘listen’ for hear — killed: contemporary diction (license ledger), hear carries śṛṇuta. Read aloud: WIDE-spreads the tan-TRĀ-lo-ka — NONE at ALL can DIVE; SO-hear THIS tan-tra-SĀ-ra … com-POSED.

lines: Wide spreads the Tantrāloka — and none at all can dive;
so hear this Tantrasāra, in plain words composed.
l4.sanskrit_cite: vitatas tantrāloko vigāhituṃ naiva śakyate sarvaiḥ | ṛjuvacanaviracitam idaṃ tu tantrasāraṃ tataḥ śṛṇuta

reads_against.argmap: Why condense, and how offered? → Vastness undiveable; therefore plain-spoken essence offered instead.
c1_essence: Mother of stainless art and new creation, five-faced Father hidden in splendor: may their yamal-burst Heart, deathless kin beyond all, flash forth; the unplungeable ocean condensed to plain essence — hear it; the heart-lotus uncontracted by the master's feet gathered for worship.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta-śānta of invocation settling into teaching
